title: Portfolio Site
short: Personal portfolio built with vanilla HTML/CSS/JS. Markdown-driven articles, dynamic content, no frameworks.
content:
## Overview

This is the site you're on right now. Built with plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No React, no build step, no framework of the week.

I wanted to actually understand what I was shipping. Frameworks hide a lot, and thats fine when you know whats underneath. But I didnt, so I went without them.



## Structure

```
index.html
article.html
src/
  main.js
  style.css
  css/
data/
  ideas.json
  projects.json
```

It loads content from JSON files based on URL params. Markdown gets rendered by marked.js, code blocks get colored by highlight.js. The homepage has a little code editor thing that uses a regex highlighter I wrote myself.

Nothing special. But its mine.

title: Kanban Board
short: Interactive kanban board with drag-and-drop, built with vanilla JS. Learning project that became a real tool.
content:
## Overview A kanban board. Drag columns, add cards, move things around. Built with nothing but vanilla HTML, CSS, and JS. Started as a learning project. I wanted to understand how drag-and-drop works without reaching for a library. Turns out the HTML5 Drag and Drop API is finicky but doable. The hard part was making it feel smooth. ### Kanban Preview ![Kanban Preview](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/218025646/610889586-f6448343-e8d0-439a-b30b-5423d065d71c.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJnaXRodWIuY29tIiwiYXVkIjoicmF3LmdpdGh1YnVzZXJjb250ZW50LmNvbSIsImtleSI6ImtleTUiLCJleHAiOjE3ODIwNjA4MDYsIm5iZiI6MTc4MjA2MDUwNiwicGF0aCI6Ii8yMTgwMjU2NDYvNjEwODg5NTg2LWY2NDQ4MzQzLWU4ZDAtNDM5YS1iMzBiLTU0MjNkMDY1ZDcxYy5wbmc_.RgNwdMceWBV0UtM0yXNpqW_ahl_Xyb-h2xhLlyawlaI) ## What it does - Add, edit, delete cards - Drag cards between columns - Everything saves to localStorage - Responsive enough to use on mobile (though I wouldnt want to) ## Why not a framework Same reason as the portfolio. title: YOLO RescueSim
short: Autonomous rescue robot simulation using ROS 2, Gazebo, and YOLOv8 for human detection.
content:
## Overview A TurtleBot3 robot navigating a disaster scene in Gazebo, using YOLOv8 to detect humans and rescue markers. ![YOLO RescueSim Preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44f22963-bd08-4449-8801-f7fd118d7409)

## How it works ``` Gazebo sim -> camera feed -> YOLOv8 detects people -> robot navigates toward them ``` The hard part was getting ROS 2 Jazzy and Gazebo Harmonic to talk to each other properly. The YOLO part was surprisingly straightforward. The navigation part was not. ## Tech - ROS 2 Jazzy - Gazebo Harmonic - YOLOv8 nano (lightweight enough to run on the simulated bot) - TurtleBot3 - Python 3.12 It works in simulation. [View on GitHub](https://github.com/ch-arslanahmad/YOLO-RescueSim)

title: School Management System
short: Console-based Java application with SQLite and PDF reports. Full CRUD for students, teachers, classes.
content:
## Overview

A console app in Java that manages students, teachers, classes, and subjects. Stores everything in SQLite, spits out PDF reports.

![School Management System Demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ch-arslanahmad/school_management_system_java/main/storage/preview-code.gif)

## What it does

Add students, assign them to classes, track teachers and subjects. The usual CRUD stuff. The PDF report generation was the interesting part. I learned more about iText than I ever wanted to.

## Tech

- Java (no frameworks, just JDBC)
- SQLite
- iText for PDFs
- java.util.logging

title: Career Counselor AI
short: Web-based AI career counseling system. Recommends degrees and subjects based on student interests.
content:
## Overview

A web app that tries to answer the question students always get stuck on: what should I study?

You tell it your interests, your strengths, your academic background. It recommends degree programs and subjects. Maybe even a road map from where you are to job-ready.

## What I have so far

- Frontend in vanilla HTML/CSS/JS
- Backend in Python (FastAPI)
- MySQL for storing profiles and recommendations
- LLM integration for the actual counseling part

The project has proper docs. SRS, architecture decisions, sprint tracking. I wanted to practice the whole software engineering pipeline, not just the coding part.

## Status

Its functional but not polished. The LLM part works but the recommendations need tuning. Still deciding whether to keep it as a portfolio piece or actually deploy it.
